_note:
document-correspondents (gap register row 5.12). A document on a case says who sent it and who it went to, and it says so by POINTING AT A PARTY OF THE CASE, never by carrying a typed-in name. The `dispatch` schema beside it keeps its ZGW Verzending meaning and becomes the per-correspondent record: one row per party a document was sent to or came from, carrying the date and the role. Two fragments rather than an edit to dossiq_register.json, per ADR-037, because several dossiq lanes build against that file at once.

🔴 WHY A UUID AND NOT A NAME. `dispatch.contactPersonName` has been in the register since the ZGW import and nothing has ever written it. A typed name cannot be counted, cannot be filtered, and goes stale the day the party is corrected: two letters to the same person read as two people. The roles `afzender` and `geadresseerde` are already in the case schema's `linkRoles`, so the party a document names is the same party the People tab renders, under the same label.

🔴 WHY THE VALUE IS A PARTY OF THIS CASE AND NOT ANY PARTY. A correspondent that is not on the case is a correspondent nobody can open, and the parties listing is the only place a handler can add one. So the writers resolve against `GET /api/objects/{r}/{s}/{id}/parties` and drop what does not match, rather than storing a uuid the People tab cannot show.

sender.title: Sender
sender.description: Who sent this document, as a party of this case in the role afzender. Holds the party's uuid, or the contact uid of a link written before the party model. An incoming document gets one from the mail intake; you can set or correct it in the document's properties.

recipients.title: Recipients
recipients.description: Who this document went to, as parties of this case in the role geadresseerde. Each entry holds the party's uuid, or the contact uid of a link written before the party model. An outgoing document gets them from the send that filed it; you can set or correct them in the document's properties.

dispatch.description: One correspondent of one document: the party a document was sent to, or the party it came from, with the date and the role. ZGW calls this a Verzending. Written by the send that files an outgoing document and by the mail intake that files an incoming one, and kept in step with `informatieobject.sender` and `informatieobject.recipients`, which are what the Files tab and the People tab read.

case.title: Case
case.description: The case this dispatch is on, so a party's correspondence can be read per case without walking every document.

involvedParty.title: Involved party
involvedParty.description: The party this dispatch names, as the uuid of a party of the case. Never a typed name: a name cannot be counted and goes stale the day the party is corrected.

relationshipType.title: Relationship type
relationshipType.description: Whether this party sent the document or received it. The two values are the case schema's own link roles, so a dispatch and the People tab name the same role.

contactPersonName.title: Contact person name
contactPersonName.description: DEPRECATED, and never written by dossiq. Kept so a record imported from a ZGW source keeps its field. Read `involvedParty` instead: the party carries the name, and it stays right when the party is corrected.
